item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is preferable because its replay change is narrower and its Upload retry coverage is stronger, though neither patch satisfies the frozen contract and A still needs substantial revision before merge.","reasons":["B globally buffers every non-replayable RawClient body and silently ignores io.ReadAll failures; after such a failure the original body may already be partially consumed, so the request can send corrupted data instead of propagating the reader error.","A includes an end-to-end Files.Upload test proving the multipart filename and content survive a 429 retry. B tests Upload encoding and tests retry elsewhere, but never verifies Upload itself retries.","A at least makes the established WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions usable with its new option interface. B creates duplicate WithAddFileQuery and WithAddFileRequestOptions machinery instead of following the existing FilesOption pattern.","Both implementations call Raw.Do directly, duplicating FilesService.Add request/response handling, rather than routing through Add as explicitly required."],"risks_a":["Upload has the wrong signature: it accepts ...UploadFileOption instead of ...FilesOption.","It adds prohibited association and arbitrary-form-field APIs and extends multipartbody unnecessarily instead of calling multipartbody.NewFile directly.","It changes public option-function return types and unrelated RawClient retry/reader-ownership behavior, creating avoidable compatibility and scope risk despite preserving Add's textual signature indirectly through the shared raw path changes its behavior beyond the contract's requested implementation pattern, effectively altering lower-level upload retry semantics instead of leaving Add untouched and routing Upload through it as specified. It also lacks a source-reader failure test and its Upload retry test uses a seekable file rather than explicitly exercising a non-seekable streamed source."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong signature (...AddFileOption), adds prohibited association fields, and introduces a parallel option system instead of keeping FilesOption behavior unchanged.","Its global buffering removes streaming for every RawClient io.Reader, can consume unbounded memory, leaks/changes ownership semantics for original ReadClosers, and cannot report buffering errors because makeBodyReplayable returns no error.","It does not test Upload retry behavior or source-reader error propagation, both required by the contract."]}
